FINDING_ID: MM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.90  
DESCRIPTION: The claimed fix for Experiment 15 item 4.1 is not actually aligned with the mathematical appendix’s ascending-abstraction guard. The appendix defines ascending abstraction using cumulative mean abstraction H̄(t), Duane rate λ(t), and the relative-rate inequality  
(dH̄/dt)/H̄(t) > |dλ/dt|/λ(t),  
with stop_valid(t) = (V̂_remaining < ε) ∧ ¬ascending_abstraction(t). The code’s fix only enforces a much weaker proxy: `_abstraction_dropping(round_idx)` compares mean abstraction of new findings in the current vs previous round (`h_curr <= h_prev`). It does not compute H̄(t), λ(t), dλ/dt, or the defining inequality. So the “FIXED” status is only true relative to an earlier missing conjunct, not true relative to the formal model stated in §7.3–7.4. This remains a model/code discrepancy and the mathematical guard is still not implemented.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either (a) weaken the appendix to document the implemented heuristic explicitly as an approximation, or preferably (b) implement the actual guard: maintain cumulative H̄(t), estimate λ(t) from round counts/durations, approximate derivatives, and evaluate the formal relative-rate inequality before allowing stop.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: Experiment 15 item 4.1’s prose resolution is internally contradictory: it says `_abstraction_dropping()` uses `<=` and describes “flat or dropping = ok to stop; ascending = keep going.” That is consistent with the code. But the line immediately before says “stop() now includes `abstraction_ok` as a conjunctive condition,” and the experiment summary labels the finding “FIXED” as if the formal appendix condition were now enforced. It is not. This is a logic/documentation mismatch in the claimed resolution status, not just a code detail.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change the resolution note to “PARTIALLY FIXED: conjunctive heuristic guard added; formal ascending-abstraction condition from appendix not implemented.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84  
DESCRIPTION: The no-fix-needed decision for Experiment 15 item 4.6 is overstated relative to the mathematical model. The appendix defines per-model and system-level yield in §7.3 as cumulative: Y(t) = N(t)·H̄(t), where H̄(t) is mean over all findings up to time t. In code, `add_model_round()` computes per-model cumulative yield by adding the current round’s `len(findings) * mean_abstraction(findings)` onto the previous total. This only equals the appendix definition if the current round input is exactly the newly added cumulative increment and if abstraction averaging is weighted compatibly over time. The implementation uses roundwise chunks of novel findings, not recomputed cumulative H̄(t) per model. So “already fixed” is too strong; it is at best an incremental surrogate, not the formal Y(t).  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reclassify the decision as “heuristic approximation accepted” unless code is changed to maintain each model’s cumulative finding set and compute Y_m(t)=N_m(t)·H̄_m(t) directly from all cumulative findings.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix’s §6 “Relationship to Other Extensions” still contains a mathematically invalid claim even after prior findings: “R_n applies directly: replace F_n with G_n in the R_n formula for combined residual risk.” This is wrong because R_n is built from per-class miss probabilities m_k and priors π_k, not from a single aggregate detection scalar. The code does not implement this substitution, which is good, but the appendix still states it. This was previously flagged, but it remains unresolved in the artifact under review.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the statement with the correct one: define combined per-class miss probability m_k^(MH) from the machine and human detection structure, then compute R_n classwise using that m_k^(MH); do not substitute aggregate G_n into R_n.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.85  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix’s §6 reduction row “K=1, d=1, uniform p → C(n)” remains under-specified and generally false for the presented G_n formula. G_n still includes separate machine/human streams and priming correlation ρ_MH. Without additional assumptions collapsing to a single homogeneous stream, it does not reduce to the baseline corroboration model C(n)=1-(1-p)^n. The code does not implement G_n, so this is a pure mathematical inconsistency in the appendix.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Narrow the reduction claim to explicit conditions, e.g. one stream only, or define n=n_M+n_H with equal per-pass independent detection and ρ_MH=0 under a unified pass model; otherwise remove the row.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix’s “All formulas in §7–8 were computationally verified using SymPy and Wolfram Alpha” is overbroad and misleading given the code and the formulas themselves. Several §7–8 claims are not formulas suitable for symbolic verification in the stated sense, and multiple internal inconsistencies remain in the same artifact (e.g. reduction claims, cross-reference semantics, undefined fallback notation, implementation-status overclaims). This is a documentation/completeness issue with epistemic status marking.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace with a scoped claim such as “Selected algebraic identities and worked examples were checked computationally; implementation correspondence and empirical validity remain separate questions.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §7.10 says “Duane NHPP (§7.1) | Verified, AICc-tested | Implemented in decay_analysis.py,” but the analytical boundary for this task requires verifying against `dynamic_management.py`. Within this code artifact, the Duane model is not implemented correctly; instead there are heuristic proxies `kappa_rate()` and `estimate_gamma()`, already known to drift from the appendix. The implementation-status table therefore creates an interface mismatch between the mathematical appendix and the code artifact actually governing runtime behaviour in this subsystem.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In §7.10, distinguish “implemented elsewhere experimentally” from “implemented in the dynamic management runtime.” State explicitly that `dynamic_management.py` currently uses heuristic convergence proxies, not the formal Duane estimator.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 3  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` for a format violation instead of `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. This is not directly a mathematical error, but it breaks the semantic distinction that the appendix and code both otherwise maintain between malformed output and format-yield problems. Because format-yield φ_i is separately formalised in the appendix, collapsing the emitted event type obscures the operational signal needed to calibrate φ_i.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION` in the FORMAT branch.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.75  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix’s termination-aware prior inflation formula remains mathematically invalid as written: π_k(exhausted)=π_k+(1−π_k)·Δ(k_max). Since Δ(k_max) is a revision count, not a probability, this can exceed 1 whenever Δ>1. The code does not implement this, but the appendix still presents it as a conservative approach. Prior finding CC2_MM_F011 identified this; it remains unresolved in the current artifact.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace Δ(k_max) with a bounded transform, e.g. δ_k = 1−exp(−c·Δ(k_max)) or normalize by total claims/pass budget so π_k(exhausted) stays in [0,1].  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix §7.4 contains a self-contradictory notation sentence: “Here k(t) is the local exponential decay rate of the sliding-window generation rate v_w(t) ... v_w(t) is the sliding-window smoothed generation rate. λ(t) is the empirical decay rate estimated from consecutive round values.” But §7.1 already defines λ(t) as the Duane NHPP intensity, not a decay rate. This sentence swaps λ(t)’s role and conflicts with the prior definition.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change the second sentence to something like: “v_w(t) is the sliding-window smoothed generation rate; k(t) is its local exponential decay parameter. This is distinct from the Duane intensity λ(t) of §7.1.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: The no-fix-needed decision for Experiment 15 item 4.3 is operationally plausible but mathematically underspecified. `_redundancy_target()` uses total pool size K, not admissible/active capacity. The resolution argues this is acceptable because greedy allocation and feasibility warnings handle infeasibility. That may be acceptable operationally, but it means the target is no longer a realizable redundancy target in the formal allocation problem; it is an aspirational upper bound. This should not be classified as “no fix needed” without updating the model statement.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reclassify as “documented design choice” and update the formal/inline docs: redundancy target uses total-pool theoretical maximum; feasibility layer may degrade realized redundancy under admissibility/capacity constraints.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: The module docstring claims “No collision with immutable symbols from §7-8 of the existing Mathematical Appendix,” explicitly listing `A`, but `CapabilityFingerprint.A` in code still uses semantics incompatible with appendix §7.9 (“Accuracy / alignment” vs “Total novel verified findings”). This is a direct contradiction between code commentary and both appendix notation and implementation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove `A` from the “no collision” claim or rename the code field to match its actual semantics; preferably align semantics to the appendix or rename the code dimension to avoid collision entirely.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F013  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: The experiment summary says “350 tests pass” as part of the justification for item 4.1 being fixed. That is not relevant evidence for conformance to the mathematical appendix unless those tests explicitly encode the formal ascending-abstraction condition. As presented, this is an epistemic overclaim: passing tests establish some behavioural correctness, not model equivalence.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Qualify the claim: “350 tests pass for the implemented heuristic stop logic; this does not by itself validate equivalence to the appendix’s formal ascending-abstraction model.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: the Exp15 “fixed” items 4.1 and 4.6 are not fully validated against the mathematical appendix, item 4.3 should not remain “no fix needed” without explicit model/documentation qualification, and multiple previously known appendix inconsistencies remain unresolved in the current artifacts.
